body_long:
In 2008, two Frenchmen opened a restaurant on Little West 12th Street, in New York's Meatpacking District. Six months later, the financial crisis hit. Bagatelle survived, then travelled. This winter, it goes home.

## Two founders, one idea

Rémi Laba and Aymeric Clemente met in New York in the early 2000s. Laba came from nightlife and took the business side. Clemente, the son of restaurant owners from Salernes in the Var, had moved to the United States at 22 and waited tables at night while holding a bank job by day.

Their idea was a long French Riviera lunch that slowly becomes a party. The concept was drawn up in 2007 and the doors opened in 2008, just before the crash.

## From Meatpacking to Pampelonne

The second address was Pampelonne beach in Saint-Tropez. The rest followed season by season: Courchevel, Mykonos, London's Mayfair on Dover Street, Saint-Barth, Dubai, Miami, Tulum, Los Cabos, Athens, Bodrum and Montauk.

Today Bagatelle Group describes itself as a collection of 15 venues, between restaurants and beach clubs. It also operates the Saint-Tropez outpost of Loulou, the Parisian brand.

The kitchens are led by Corporate Chef Rocco Seminara, trained under Alain Ducasse, with years at the Hôtel de Paris Monte-Carlo and the Hôtel Martinez in Cannes. Manon Santini signs the pastry.

## A busy year

Bagatelle Miami River opened on 21 November 2025, on the river with its own dock, with Executive Chef Marco Antonio Estrada Gallardo. Bagatelle Malta, at St George's Bay, was due to open on 31 October 2026 with the local Lifestyle Group: about 1,960 square metres, a restaurant for more than 180 guests and a beach club, with Executive Chef Walter D'Ambrosio.

Then the homecoming. Bagatelle has announced a new New York address at 413-419 West 14th Street, a few blocks from the original, opening in winter 2026. "The homecoming. A new chapter," the brand wrote. Lisbon and San Juan are listed as coming soon.

## The signal

Bagatelle does not sell a dish. It sells an atmosphere that can be reproduced from the Alps to the Caribbean, often with a local partner: Lifestyle Group in Malta, Mandala Group and The Dirty Rabbit Group in Miami.

For hotels, that is the lesson. A strong restaurant and beach club brand can bring a crowd, a season and a name to a destination that a hotel alone struggles to build.
summary: From a Meatpacking restaurant opened just before the 2008 crash to 15 venues worldwide, the story of Bagatelle, which returns to New York this winter.
